text:
morgan: heads-up — got a paid customer (acme-corp) reporting intermittent 502/504s hitting the hosted inference API in eu-west-1 since ~08:12Z. morgan: they've attached a few request ids, main example: trace=tr_0a9b8c7d, client ts 2026-03-15T08:13:02Z
alex: linking the logs now. are we seeing any host-level oom or GPU errors?
jin: quick paste from edge logs around tr_0a9b8c7d:
```
"[2026-03-15T08:13:02Z] envoy error: upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers. uri: /v1/generate, upstream: 10.12.45.67:8080, cluster: hosted-api-eu-west, response_code: 502
```
jin: also seeing repeated auth cache misses right before the 502s, e.g. 'auth: cache miss user:acct-9983' and short TTL refresh bursts.
sarah: customer says errors spike after they rotate their API key via our console — could be an auth cache thundering herd after rotation.
leo: that would explain the timing. when keys rotate we invalidate auth cache entries which can cause a lot of upstream auth calls. if too many upstream calls hit the auth manager it can saturate the auth-service connections and cascade to 502s from edge.
alex: can someone paste envoy upstream log lines with connection error types? need to confirm if it's connect timeout vs conn reset.
jin: more lines:
```
"[2026-03-15T08:13:03Z] envoy info: upstream response timeout from 10.12.45.67:8080
"[2026-03-15T08:13:04Z] envoy warn: remote reset before headers
```
jin: so mixed: some upstream timeouts, some resets. pattern looks like short window of auth backend saturation + h2 pool exhaustion between edge and our auth-service/router.
morgan: customer repro steps (from their support ticket):
1) rotate API key in console
2) immediately fire 50 concurrent requests using the old SDK (which retries)
3) ~20% of requests see 502 or 504 for ~30s
morgan: they've included a minimal repro curl loop:
```
for i in {1..50}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <new-or-old-key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait
```
morgan: they said errors stop after ~30s as the new key populates caches.
leo: likely causes: auth cache invalidation + upstream connections/spike to auth-service, plus h2 connection pool (keepalive) exhaustion to model backends if requests were retried heavily.
alex: mitigation ideas? short-term: we can opt to 1) warm the auth cache proactively on rotation, 2) temporarily increase h2 pool size for hosted-api-eu-west, 3) add a short 429/backoff for bursts post-rotation to prevent retry storms.
jin: I can patch the auth-manager to jitter TTL rebuilds (randomized backoff on cache repop). quickly we can also enable fail-open behavior for auth checks for 10s for partner-tier customers to avoid 502 cascade — but that's risky.
sarah: customer asks for immediate workaround — can we suggest they wait 60s after rotation before doing bulk requests? they'll likely want us to fix on our side.
morgan: I'm escalating to eng-sre with priority P2 since customer is paid and seeing degraded latency/5xx. tagging @alex @jin @leo.
deploy-bot: release candidate 2026.03.15-rc5 deployed to staging at 08:40Z — no changes yet to auth-manager.
alex: ops ask — can someone check connection pool metrics from edge->auth-service between 08:10-08:20Z (datadog dashboard)? I'm specifically after active connections, wait_count, and pool_exhausted events.
jin: pulled metrics: pool_exhausted spikes from 0 -> 120 for cluster auth-svc-eu-west at 08:12Z, active connections saturate to configured limit 200, then resets as cache warms.
leo: that confirms h2 pool exhaustion. also see a 10x increase in auth-service latency (p95 jumped 200ms->1.2s) which explains upstream timeouts.
alex: immediate mitigations applied: increased auth-svc max_connections from 200 -> 400 for eu-west cluster (will roll at 08:50Z). also applied short rate-limit on edge for bursty requests from single IP to reduce retry storms.
ops-bot: auth-svc-eu-west config change scheduled: increase max_conns=400, rollout window 08:50Z-08:53Z.
morgan: customer confirmed errors dropped after 09:00Z and their repro no longer causes 502s. they still want a permanent fix so it doesn't recur during scheduled rotations.
jin: proposed longer-term fixes:
- jittered cache repopulation on key rotation (avoid simultaneous cache refetch)
- progressive invalidation: mark old key stale but allow short grace period for concurrent requests
- increase default h2 pool size and make pool autoscale based on wait_count signals
- instrument rotation flow to warm caches proactively for customer accounts doing rotation via UI/CLI
alex: agree. let's create a follow-up RFC and schedule a 2-week engineering ticket: AUTH-4823 (thundering-auth-cache + pool autoscale).
morgan: customer comms: I'll send a summary with what we did and planned fixes. they asked for an SLA credit — forwarding to CS manager.
sarah: also add test coverage: simulate key rotation + 100 concurrent client retries in staging to validate.
leo: final note: watch for similar patterns in other regions when customers rotate keys en masse (automation/CI). we should add a dashboard alert: "Auth cache miss spike + pool_exhausted > 30s => paging".
morgan: thanks team. closing thread when RFC/issue scheduled. tagging @jin to own the immediate jitter patch. :thumbsup:
jin: on it — will open PR for jittered repop by EOD and link here.
deploy-bot: PR merged to staging: auth-jitter-PR#412 at 10:12Z — staging smoke looks good.
morgan: resolved for now — customer updated and happy. follow-ups: AUTH-4823 + dashboard alert.
alex: adding runbook note: 'on customer key rotation spikes, check auth-service pool_exhausted, increase conn limit temporarily, and coordinate with CS to pause bulk requests.' saved to runbooks/edge-auth-rotations.
morgan: thread closed.
